risk_if_not_implemented: Without Third-Party Exit Contingencies, termination of a third-party relationship may interrupt operations with no fallback, leaving security, compliance and continuity dependent on a provider that is no longer engaged. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Business / Service Interruption (R-BC-1), Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-5), Recovery Failure / Unacceptable Recovery Delay (R-OR-1), Concentration / Single-Point Dependency Failure (R-OR-2), Third-Party Dependency Failure (R-SC-6), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Supplier Financial Distress / Insolvency (MT-24).

compensating_control_1.name: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) Plans
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist for process owners to establish and maintain formal Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) plans to ensure information is detailed enough, accurate and representative of current operations in order to sustain and/or restore operations under adverse conditions.
compensating_control_1.justification: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) Plans (BCD-04) compensates for the absence of Third-Party Exit Contingencies (TPM-24.7) by maintaining Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) plans that define how critical services are sustained through disruption, which provides the operational fallback an exit contingency would specify. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Supplier Diversity
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to obtain security, compliance and resilience technologies from different suppliers to minimize supply chain risk.
compensating_control_2.justification: Supplier Diversity (TPM-06) compensates for the absence of Third-Party Exit Contingencies (TPM-24.7) by maintaining alternative suppliers for security, compliance and resilience technologies, which reduces the single-point dependency that makes an unplanned exit disruptive. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
